policy: Learn from observed video evidence, identify root cause, make small testable improvements to common policy/templates/code, verify, then reuse next time. Never assert perfect quality or invent user feedback, analytics, or tests.
highSeverityRule: CRITICAL and MAJOR require FIXED with checked changed files and verification before review closes. MINOR can be BACKLOG with a reason and owner.
strongRules: Watch/listen to the whole final MP4 and note timestamped strengths and defects.
Separate observable symptom from hypothesized cause; do not confidently diagnose from screenshots alone.
When an error reveals a systematic failure, improve shared template/policy/validator, not only a single video's prompt.
Retest the specific error and run repo tests. No unverified improvement claims.
Do not overfit to one video's taste; hold experiments separately until replicated.
Preserve simple 2D stickman world, without real human appearance; figures only when helpful.
Quality means clarity and accuracy, not maximum movement, character count or label count.
Learn from both mistakes and successful sections.
No new project while a locally rendered prior video has an unfinished review.
Analytics must be explicitly provided or available from a connected source; no invented numbers.
analyticsPolicy: Optional post-publication update after YouTube Studio data exists (typically 1–2 days for retention); compare context and video length, do not treat CTR or a spike as proof of one cause.

references.label: YouTube Help: audience retention (intro, dips, spikes)
YouTube Help: interpreting CTR and impressions

visualQcPolicy.limitation: Gate validates signed-off reviewer attestations and PNG hashes, NOT visual pixel meaning.
